title: Singing Dads Become Surprise Stars Online
summary:
A group of singers near Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, became famous online without even trying.

The group is called the Tonics. They sing a cappella, which means without instruments. Most of the 18 members are dads and grandfathers. They practice in each other's kitchens.

Last year, the Tonics had about 500 followers on Instagram. Then, in December, they posted a video of themselves singing the song "Drift Away." It got 300,000 views! One later video got more than 4 million views.

"We were shocked," said Youngmoo Kim, the group's music director.

An online star named Emilie Hagen helped share their videos. She said the Tonics felt "authentic and wholesome."

The group started in 1990 with friends from school. Today, they have almost 100,000 followers. They plan to release four new songs on Spotify later this year.

Kim's advice is simple: just be yourself.
why_it_matters: The Tonics show kids that doing what you love and being yourself can make others happy too.

keywords.explanation: A cappella means singing with only voices and no instruments.
Instruments are things used to make music, like pianos and guitars.
Followers are people who sign up to see someone's posts online.
A music director leads a music group and helps it practice.
Authentic means real and true, not fake.
Wholesome means good and nice for everyone.
